kept.excerpt: Lindell leads the Republican gubernatorial primary by 9 points, with 35 percent of support, according to the poll. House Speaker Lisa Demuth is in second place with 26 percent, and GOP-endorsed Kendall Qualls is in third with 11 percent. Twenty-two percent of respondents were undecided.
kept.relevance: The latest verified pre-cutoff polling report places Lindell ahead but shows a substantial undecided electorate.

kept.excerpt: Lindell has raised over $726,000 in campaign donations this year, and his campaign had $88,000 in cash as of July 20, according to the campaign’s latest finance report. Demuth has the most cash on hand compared to her Republican primary opponents, with over $456,000. The campaign has raised over $550,000 this year. Qualls’ campaign has over $67,000 in cash and has raised over $410,000 this year.
kept.relevance: The final pre-primary finance reporting shows Demuth holding a substantial cash advantage over Lindell despite his larger fundraising total.

kept.excerpt: President Donald Trump has endorsed MyPillow founder Mike Lindell for Minnesota governor, praising him as “one of America's greatest and most hard working Patriots” and giving formal backing to a fellow election denier a day before the Republican president delivers a national address he says will focus on election security. Lindell’s primary opponents include state House Speaker Lisa Demuth and businessman Kendall Qualls, who has the endorsement of the Minnesota state GOP.
kept.relevance: Trump’s endorsement provides Lindell a major source of Republican support while the state party backs a competing candidate.

kept.excerpt: Minnesota Republicans spent almost a half-day and needed 10 ballots Saturday to endorse former health executive Kendall Qualls for governor, putting him in a strong position to be the party’s fall candidate if he can survive a summer primary. Qualls won at a GOP convention plagued by problematic vote clickers that left some rivals doubting the process. Just after 9 p.m., he surpassed the 60 percent threshold in a head-to-head showdown over lone remaining opponent, House Speaker Lisa Demuth.
kept.relevance: The convention result establishes Qualls’ organizational backing and distinguishes the party endorsement from the binding primary election.

kept.excerpt: Voting in Minnesota’s August 11, 2026 Primary Election will begin on June 26, 2026. In the primary, voters choose candidates to appear on the November 3 General Election ballot.
kept.publisher: Office of the Minnesota Secretary of State
kept.relevance: The official announcement confirms the primary schedule and that voting was already underway before the evidence cutoff.

kept.excerpt: A political action committee associated with Demuth has received about $1.1 million from a national PAC largely funded by Uihlein. The funding has given her a significant advantage over her two gubernatorial primary opponents: GOP-endorsed candidate Kendall Qualls and MyPillow CEO Mike Lindell. Restore Sanity has spent over $1 million in television and digital advertisements and mailing material in the past six months in favor of Demuth’s campaign for governor, according to campaign finance data.
kept.relevance: Outside advertising support strengthens Demuth’s ability to compete with Lindell beyond the resources in her own campaign account.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-07-30.
